problems.source_says: Participants produced the image-replication attempts using the provided generative model. The form retains this as an output-scored usefulness outcome with AI available. Applying codebook section 1, that combination requires with_ai; none is not a permitted question under the stated routing rule. The fixed-target nature of S1 supports the form's substantive exclusion from creative-task eligibility, but does not create an exception to the question rule. If S1 is retained only as out-of-scope context, that distinction should be recorded outside the routed outcome estimates.
problems.quote: In the image replication experiment, participants were asked to replicate a “target image” as closely as possible using the generative model provided to them.
problems.locator: PDF p. 10, sections 3.2 and 3.2.1; p. 11, continuation of section 3.2.1; creativity-codebook.md, section 1 (Scope, question-routing paragraph).

confirmed.statement: S2-O1 is scored on generated logos, not self-reports: an LLM compares how well two images satisfy the brief, and Bradley-Terry strengths summarize those judgments.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 11-12, sections 3.3-3.3.1; pp. 49-50, Appendix D.2.

confirmed.statement: S2-O1 construct usefulness and measure automated_score are supported by the client-requirements judging instruction and use of gpt-4.1-nano at temperature 0.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 49-50, Appendix D.2; creativity-codebook.md, section 6.

confirmed.statement: S2-O1 has an output analysis unit: each image receives a strength parameter used in the treatment-effect regressions; the judging pairs are not the regression observations, and standard errors cluster by participant.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 50, Appendix D.2; pp. 57-59, Appendix F.1.3-F.2.4, equations 13-14.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 uses computed CLIP similarity to a fixed target, averaged over 10 generated images per prompt. Its main analysis is at the participant-prompt level; the form correctly describes this as expected fidelity/quality rather than cross-person diversity.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 10-11, section 3.2.1; pp. 49 and 54, Appendices D.1 and E.3; pp. 55-57, Appendix F.1.1-F.1.3.

confirmed.statement: AI was available during both participant tasks. S2-O1 therefore routes to with_ai; subsequent researcher replay of existing prompts is not an after_ai participant test.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, section 3.1; p. 13, section 3.4; pp. 44-45, Appendix C.3; creativity-codebook.md, section 1.

confirmed.statement: The recorded n_units values, 18,560 for S1 and 18,425 for S2, match the retained all-arm prompt counts, as the form explicitly qualifies; they are not pairwise-judgment counts or contrast-specific regression sample sizes.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 46-47, Appendices C.4-C.5; p. 57, Appendix F.1.3.

confirmed.statement: All S1-O1 reported main-text effect sizes, confidence intervals, p-values, replay shares, and Table 1 coefficients/SEs match the PDF, including the 0.0164 ATE and 58% reduction in the upgrade benefit.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 14-17, sections 4.1.1-4.1.4, Figures 1-2 and Table 1.

confirmed.statement: All S1-O1 reported DreamSim and CLIP Z-score robustness numbers match the PDF. The description of Revised versus DALL-E 2 first/average/best performance also matches the appendix.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 63-64, Appendices H.1.1, H.1.3, H.2.1 and H.2.3; pp. 75-76, Appendix I.1, H5.

confirmed.statement: All S2-O1 reported main-text and Table 2 numbers match the PDF, including ATE 0.8075, CI [0.7120, 0.9030], replay effects 0.748 and 0.0577, and the reverse-replay effect -0.0125.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 18-21, sections 4.2.1-4.2.4, Figures 3-4 and Table 2.

confirmed.statement: S2-O1 correctly preserves Revised versus DALL-E 2 as 0.8337 in the main text and 0.834 with CI [0.7358, 0.9316] in Appendix F; its reported Z-score estimates and p-values also match.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 20, section 4.2.4; p. 58, Appendix F.2.1; pp. 64-65, Appendices H.3.1 and H.3.3.

confirmed.statement: Tables 1-2 concern the distribution of output quality, not content diversity. Successive and aggregate prompt similarity compare each person with their own prompts; they do not establish across_people outcomes.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 17 and 21, Tables 1-2; pp. 50-52, Appendices D.4-D.8; pp. 56 and 59, Appendices F.1.2 and F.2.2.

confirmed.statement: The full document, including Appendices A-I, supplies no additional reported treatment effect on final-output creativity/diversity or unassisted post-AI output that is missing from the form; the other measures describe prompting behavior or variants of the recorded quality scores.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 1-84; especially pp. 50-52, Appendix D.3-D.8; pp. 63-65, Appendix H; pp. 66-84, Appendix I.

confirmed.statement: Human logo-validation ratings are mentioned for approximately 19,000 image pairs, but no human-rated treatment-effect estimate is supplied.

summary: S1-O1's question='none' violates the stated routing rule for an AI-available usefulness outcome, which requires with_ai. Eligibility holds because S2 scores participants' generated logos for client-brief fulfillment; the recorded numerical results match the PDF.
